transcript.text: My Samsung dishwasher DW60M6050FS keeps showing 4C and beeping, won't do anything

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. On Samsung dishwashers, 4C means a water supply fault. The machine tried to fill but little or no fresh water came in within the time it expects, so it stops and beeps. Most of the time it's something simple on the supply side rather than a failed part. - The inlet (fill) valve has failed or is only letting a trickle through. This is less likely and is only worth suspecting once the supply is proven good. 1. Find the tap the dishwasher hose connects to, usually under the sink, and make sure it's fully open. Follow the hose back and check it isn't kinked or flattened, especially if the machine has been pushed back recently. If it was off or kinked, that alone is probably your fault.
2. If the hose has a plastic box near the tap end (an AquaStop), check whether its little window shows red. Red means the safety valve has tripped and the hose usually needs replacing.
3. Turn the tap off, put a towel down and have a small bowl handy. Unscrew the hose at the back of the dishwasher and look into the inlet for a small mesh filter. If it's clogged, rinse it clean under a tap; a cocktail stick or old toothbrush helps. A blocked mesh is a common cause, especially in hard-water areas.
4. Refit the hose firmly, turn the tap back on, check for drips, then plug in and start a programme. Listen for water coming in within the first minute or so. If the tap, hose and filter are all fine and it still shows 4C with no water coming in (or just a trickle), the inlet valve becomes the main suspect, and we can talk through what that involves. How did those checks go?

The valve under the sink had a screwdriver slot and it was turned to 90 degrees, so it was off. I turned it on and the dishwasher now fills and runs normally. No kinks in the hose, and the water pressure at the kitchen tap is fine. I didn't check the filter.

That's sorted, then. The isolation valve was off, so the dishwasher couldn't get any water, and 4C is exactly how it reports that. With the valve open it's filling and running normally, so nothing is faulty. A quick tip for next time: that type of valve is open when the screwdriver slot lines up with the pipe and closed when it sits across the pipe at 90 degrees. They get knocked or turned off during plumbing work or when things are moved around under the sink, so if 4C ever comes back, check the slot first. You don't need to bother with the inlet filter now it's filling properly. If you ever notice it starting to fill slowly, that mesh where the hose screws on is the next thing to clean, especially in a hard-water area. Is there anything else I can help with?

claimsRejected.claim: - The tap feeding the dishwasher is off or only partly open, or the inlet hose is kinked or squashed behind the machine.
- The small mesh filter where the hose screws onto the dishwasher is blocked with grit or scale.
If it fills normally after this, you've found it.

candidates: Water supply problem: tap off or partly closed, kinked inlet hose, or AquaStop tripped (high)
Blocked inlet mesh filter where the hose connects (medium)

tags.checkGiven: Check the tap the dishwasher hose connects to is fully on, the hose isn't kinked behind the machine, and if the hose has an AquaStop box at

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Samsung; model DW60M6050FS; code 4C.
The fault they reported is: "shows 4C error, beeping, won't run". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.

candidates: Water supply isolation valve was turned off (high)
plan: The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.

facts.value: supply valve under sink: was turned off (90 degrees); turned on, dishwasher now fills and runs normally
water pressure at kitchen tap: fine

asked.resolution: Supply valve was off; turned on, now fills and runs normally
